scope.coverage: All public def/theorem declarations from the actual module, in source order. No inventory or author classification consulted.

ambient_definitions.PrimitiveBasis: abbrev PrimitiveBasis (qubits : Nat) := Fin qubits → Fin 2. Type, not a Hilbert-space vector or complex amplitude array. A function assigning a 0/1 value to each named finite wire.
ambient_definitions.gridSize: def gridSize (n : Nat) : Nat := 2 ^ n. Fin (gridSize q) means natural values < 2^q, with proof fields.
ambient_definitions.OtherPrimitiveWires: abbrev OtherPrimitiveWires {qubits : Nat} (target : Fin qubits) := {wire : Fin qubits // wire ≠ target}. The width is implicit in this imported alias only.
ambient_definitions.splitPrimitiveWire: def splitPrimitiveWire {qubits : Nat} (target : Fin qubits) : PrimitiveBasis qubits ≃ Fin 2 × (OtherPrimitiveWires target → Fin 2). Forward state ↦ (state target, wire ↦ state wire.val); inverse pair at wire is pair.1 if wire=target, otherwise pair.2 ⟨wire, wire≠target⟩. The context is a function on a subtype of named wires, not intrinsically a flat number.
ambient_definitions.equivalence: Equiv supplies forward/inverse functions plus both inverse laws; applying or taking .symm uses its function coercion. All equivalences in the target module are between fixed Type-level finite carriers. Equality of bit/context functions is extensional equality.
ambient_definitions.Fin_consEquiv: {n : Nat} → (α : Fin (n+1) → Type u) → (α 0 × ((i : Fin n) → α i.succ)) ≃ ((i : Fin (n+1)) → α i). Symmetric use separates head and tail.
ambient_definitions.finProdFinEquiv: {m n : Nat} → Fin m × Fin n ≃ Fin (m*n); (a,b) ↦ b.val + n*a.val; inverse index ↦ (index.divNat,index.modNat). In the target successor construction, m=2^q and n=2 after prodComm. Omitting that swap would change the convention.
ambient_definitions.prodCongr_prodComm_finCongr: prodCongr maps both factors through supplied equivalences; prodComm swaps factors; finCongr transports a Fin value across an equality of bounds without changing its natural value. The final bound is (2^q)*2=2^(q+1), discharged by simp [gridSize,pow_succ].
ambient_definitions.nat_operations: All coordinate /,% ,+,* and powers are natural arithmetic, not integer, modular-register or complex operations. Fin wire/index constraints are built into the types; modulo-bit bound witnesses generated by omega are not mathematical premises.

exact_convention.indexing: Ascending named wire number means ascending binary significance: wire j has weight 2^j. The successor rule and zero case determine this for every natural width.
exact_convention.semantic_sum_inference: By iterating the recursive equation, encode_q(bits).val is Σ_{j=0}^{q-1} 2^j*bits(j).val. This is an independent semantic consequence, not a named arbitrary-width sum theorem in this module.
exact_convention.inverse_inference: Recursion gives bit j=(index.val / 2^j)%2. Explicit named inverse formulas are provided only at widths 2 and 3.
exact_convention.context_codes: Two-wire codes lie in 0..1; three-wire codes in 0..3, by their definitions and bounded input. The declared return type is Nat, not Fin 2/Fin 4, and no standalone range theorem is declared.
exact_convention.equality_not_state_action: Context iff results compare all surviving coordinates exactly and impose no condition on the target coordinate. They do not prove a gate action, amplitudes, permutation-matrix reindexing or physical reversal of wires.

legal_cases.zero_width: q=0 is expressly legal: Fin 0 has no wires, PrimitiveBasis 0 has exactly one empty function, gridSize 0=1 and Fin 1 has only index 0. The inverse is Fin.elim0, not an empty index space. A target : Fin 0 cannot be supplied to splitPrimitiveWire.
legal_cases.width_one: q=1 is legal in the generic equivalence and successor theorem; values 0/1 encode the sole bit. There is no named width-one inverse/context lemma here; its non-target function would have empty domain if splitPrimitiveWire were applied.
legal_cases.arbitrary_width: All q : Nat are allowed, without q>0, q≥2, q≥3, q≥6, powers-of-two promises or oracle assumptions beyond the defined 2^q carrier. The six-value theorem is exactly width 6.
legal_cases.fixed_two_three: Fixed inverse/context lemmas take only widths 2 and 3, every legal index (4 or 8), and every legal target (2 or 3). No distinct-control/target premise, boundary restriction, left≠right, or target-bit agreement is required. Default target/wire pattern branches select 1 for Fin 2 and 2 for Fin 3, not an out-of-range case.

declarations.name: QuantumBlockEncoding.primitiveBasisLEEquiv
declarations.exact_surface_signature: def primitiveBasisLEEquiv : (q : Nat) -> PrimitiveBasis q ≃ Fin (gridSize q)
declarations.decoded_statement: For every natural width q, an invertible coordinate map between total bit assignments and flat indices below 2^q. Zero maps the unique empty assignment to index 0. Successor splits head bit and tail, maps the tail recursively, swaps (bit,tailIndex) to (tailIndex,bit), and flattens as bit + 2*tailIndex. Inverse divides by 2 for tail index and takes remainder modulo 2 for head bit, recursively.
